- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (avg between -0.2 and +0.2), model frequently underestimates upward momentum → add 2–3% buffer to forecast for bullish momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead) → apply slight upward bias (1–2%) for short-term horizon.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (avg > +0.3) and price is near 30-day low, model often fails to capture rally → increase forecast by 3–5% to reflect sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 2–3 days → adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment turning points.
